blocks.prompt: 5 A sound has intensity \(I = 10^{-6}\ \text{W/m}^2\) and reference intensity \(I_0 = 10^{-12}\ \text{W/m}^2\). Find the sound level in decibels.
blocks.explanation:
A direct decibel question: both intensities are given.
We must find the sound level \(L\).
Plan: substitute into \(L = 10\log\left(\frac{I}{I_0}\right)\), simplify the power of 10, then use \(\log(10^{x}) = x\).
steps:
Given: \(I = 10^{-6}\), \(I_0 = 10^{-12}\) (both in \(\text{W/m}^2\)).
To find: the sound level \(L\) in dB.
Method: the decibel formula \(L = 10\log\left(\frac{I}{I_0}\right)\), with \(\log\) to base 10.

Substitute the values
\[L = 10\log\left(\dfrac{10^{-6}}{10^{-12}}\right)\]
Why: \(I\) on top, \(I_0\) underneath.

Take the logarithm
\[L = 10\log(10^{6})\]
\[= 10 \times 6 = 60\ \text{dB}\]
Why: \(\log(10^{6}) = 6\) for base 10.

Check
\[10^{60/10} = 10^{6} = \dfrac{I}{I_0} \;\checkmark\]
Why: 60 dB means \(10^{6}\) times the threshold intensity, which is the ratio we started with.
